t.E426.agn: In 2017 EFSA saw no need for a numerical acceptable daily intake (ADI) and stated that a safety concern at the current use is very unlikely. EFSA recommended that residual proteins in the additive be reduced as far as possible and that consumers be informed about possible allergenic proteins.
t.E426.body: Soybean hemicellulose is not absorbed intact; it is largely fermented by gut bacteria.
t.E426.eff.0.t: Residual soy proteins may cause an allergic reaction; in the EU it is indicated on the label as a soy allergen
t.E426.eval: It is obtained from soy (relevant for people with soy allergy).
t.E426.found.0: In the EU, permitted in many foods at quantum satis (as much as needed)
t.E426.found.1: Flavoured fermented milk products and flavoured drinks
t.E426.prod: It is obtained from soy fibre by hot-water extraction.
t.E426.pw.0: It is obtained from soy; EFSA stated that possibly allergenic soy proteins may remain in the additive.
t.E426.regx.0: Re-evaluated; no numerical ADI needed. Reduction of residual soy proteins was recommended.
t.E426.regx.1: Use was extended to cover flavoured fermented milk products and flavoured drinks (Group I).
t.E426.regx.2: Soybeans and soy products (except for exemptions such as fully refined oil) must be emphasised in the list of ingredients.
t.E426.summary: A fibre obtained from soybeans. It provides thickness and stability in products such as drinks and noodles.
t.E426.what: It thickens and keeps the mixture stable by preventing proteins from precipitating in acidic conditions.
